name: Hannah
charge: Praying in bitterness of soul, vowing a son to the Lord, and giving him when she had him
summary: Barren, provoked yearly by her rival, mistaken for a drunkard by the high priest, she poured out her soul before the Lord and vowed that if he gave her a son she would give him back for all his days. He did, and she did: she brought Samuel to Shiloh as soon as he was weaned. The Lord gave her five more.
offense: Hannah's barrenness was made bitter by repeated provocation. Year by year, when the household went up to worship, her adversary vexed her until she wept and would not eat (1 Samuel 1:4-7). She brought that sorrow before the Lord and vowed that, if he gave her a son, she would give him to the Lord all his days, with no razor upon his head (1 Samuel 1:9-11). The words joined her petition to the separation described in Numbers 6:5. Eli saw her moving lips without hearing her voice and thought her drunk. She answered that she had poured out her soul before the Lord, and he sent her away in peace. She then ate, and her countenance was no more sad (1 Samuel 1:12-18). Her faith was shown before the birth, when she went from prayer able to receive food again. Being misunderstood by the priest did not turn her from the one to whom she had prayed. First John 5:14-15 joins confidence in prayer to asking according to the Lord's will; First John 3:22 joins receiving to keeping his commandments and doing what pleases him. Hannah's answer came in the Lord's time. Prayer did not put the timing of the gift under her control. She entrusted the petition to him and afterward named her son in remembrance of what she had asked (1 Samuel 1:19-20). When Samuel was weaned, she brought him to Shiloh with the offerings and presented him to Eli. The child she had wanted was the child she now gave for lifelong service (1 Samuel 1:24-28). Ecclesiastes 5:4-6 commands the payment of a vow instead of dismissing it as an error. Hannah did not treat answered prayer as the end of her obligation. She performed the promise when its fulfilment required parting with the son she loved.
judgment: Samuel ministered before the Lord, and Hannah brought him a little coat each year. Her dedication did not become forgetfulness; she continued to supply the care she could give (1 Samuel 2:18-19). Eli blessed the household, and the Lord visited her with three sons and two daughters (1 Samuel 2:20-21). The one son was not withheld, and her house received five more. Her song declares that the Lord is a God of knowledge and that actions are weighed by him (1 Samuel 2:3). Her own conduct had joined prayer, promise, and performance. Christ's question—why call him Lord and not do what he says—reaches the same distinction between profession and obedience (Luke 6:46). The words spoken before God are to be followed by the life promised to him. The song passes from her household to the Lord's rule over strength, riches, life, and death. He brings low and lifts up; by strength no man prevails; he gives strength to his king and exalts his anointed (1 Samuel 2:4-10). Hannah's joy therefore ends in the Lord's salvation, not her own victory over the woman who provoked her. The gift was his, the service was his, and the glory remained his.

verses.text: So Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and after they had drunk. Now Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the Lord.
And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the Lord, and wept sore.

And she vowed a vow, and said, O Lord of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.
And it came to pass, as she continued praying before the Lord, that Eli marked her mouth.
Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken.
And Eli said unto her, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee.
And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the Lord.
Count not thine handmaid for a daughter of Belial: for out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.
Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.
And she said, Let thine handmaid find grace in thy sight. So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad.
And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before the Lord, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah: and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the Lord remembered her.
Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the Lord.

And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bullocks, and one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine, and brought him unto the house of the Lord in Shiloh: and the child was young.
And they slew a bullock, and brought the child to Eli.
And she said, Oh my lord, as thy soul liveth, my lord, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto the Lord.
For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him:
Therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord. And he worshipped the Lord there.
And Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the Lord, mine horn is exalted in the Lord: my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; because I rejoice in thy salvation.
There is none holy as the Lord: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.
Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.
They that were full have hired out themselves for bread; and they that were hungry ceased: so that the barren hath born seven; and she that hath many children is waxed feeble.
The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up.
The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.

He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them.
He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail.

The adversaries of the Lord shall be broken to pieces; out of heaven shall he thunder upon them: the Lord shall judge the ends of the earth; and he shall give strength unto his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed.
But Samuel ministered before the Lord, being a child, girded with a linen ephod.
Moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said, The Lord give thee seed of this woman for the loan which is lent to the Lord. And they went unto their own home.
And the Lord visited Hannah, so that she conceived, and bare three sons and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew before the Lord.
And Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground.
And all Israel from Dan even to Beer–sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord.
And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh: for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the Lord.
When thou shalt vow a vow unto the Lord thy God, thou shalt not slack to pay it: for the Lord thy God will surely require it of thee; and it would be sin in thee.
But if thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee.
That which is gone out of thy lips thou shalt keep and perform; even a freewill offering, according as thou hast vowed unto the Lord thy God, which thou hast promised with thy mouth.

entries.commentary: There was a certain man of mount Ephraim named Elkanah, and he had two wives: the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children. Elkanah went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the Lord of hosts in Shiloh, where the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the Lord, were. Shiloh is another name for Jerusalem.

When Elkanah offered, he gave to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters portions; but unto Hannah he gave a worthy portion, for he loved Hannah: but the Lord had shut up her womb. Her adversary provoked her sore, to make her fret, because the Lord had shut up her womb; year by year, when she went up to the house of the Lord, she provoked her, so that Hannah wept and did not eat. The women of Israel have not changed one bit: even back in the times of Samuel there was a sister vexing a barren woman and rubbing it in her face. Sisters of Israel have to get their spirits right; no doubt about it, you are Israel.
Elkanah her husband said to her, Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons?

Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and in bitterness of soul she prayed unto the Lord and wept sore, while Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the Lord. She vowed a vow: O Lord of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and there shall no rasor come upon his head. What law is that going back to? The law of the Nazarite. Put some things together as you read through Samuel about Samuel.

As she continued praying before the Lord, Eli marked her mouth. Hannah spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken, and said, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee. Hannah answered, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the Lord; count not thine handmaid for a daughter of Belial. Then Eli answered, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him. So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad. What did she do? She believed when she heard the word of Eli. Why did the Lord grant her petition? It was the will of the Most High for Samuel to come through Hannah; it was just in his time. And she was granted it because of what she did before she even asked: she kept his commandments and did those things that are pleasing in his sight.

They rose up in the morning early, worshipped before the Lord, and returned to their house to Ramah; they went back up north, for Elkanah came out of mount Ephraim. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife: knew means he laid with her, they had laid down together; and the Lord remembered her. When the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, she bare a son and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the Lord. Samuel means asked of the Lord.
The man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer unto the Lord the yearly sacrifice, and his vow. What is that yearly sacrifice going into? [Deuteronomy 16:16](/bible/deuteronomy/16#v16).

But Hannah went not up; she said unto her husband, I will not go up until the child be weaned, and then I will bring him, that he may appear before the Lord, and there abide for ever. A weaned child was three or four years old; that would be the last time he was under her care, so she said, I am not going up until that happens. Elkanah said unto her, Do what seemeth thee good; tarry until thou have weaned him; only the Lord establish his word. She did not have to go up: the law said all thy males. So the woman abode, and gave her son suck until she weaned him.

When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bullocks, and one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine, and brought him unto the house of the Lord in Shiloh: and the child was young. She said to Eli, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto the Lord. For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him: therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord. That is great faith right there that Hannah had, and she kept her promise: Hannah was an upright and honest woman.

Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the Lord, mine horn is exalted in the Lord: I rejoice in thy salvation. There is none holy as the Lord: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.

Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. What the Lord weighs is actions: if it came out of your mouth, are you going to do it? All of us in this walk, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, have taken covenant and proclaimed out of our mouths that we are going to endure to the end; we broke the bread and drank the wine and took the covenant with the Lord. Now the Lord is judging you by your actions: are you going to endure to the end, whether to Christ's return or until you leave this earth, if you truly love him?
The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. The Lord is prophesying through Hannah here.
The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The Lord decides who wakes up and the Lord decides who passes; that is all of the Lord.
The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.

He raiseth up the poor out of the dust: out of the dust means out of confusion; he brings the poor out of confusion, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord's, and he hath set the world upon them.

He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail. The adversaries of the Lord shall be broken to pieces; and he shall give strength unto his king, which is Christ, and exalt the horn of his anointed.

Elkanah went to Ramah to his house, and the child did minister unto the Lord before Eli the priest. Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the Lord. They were the devil. They were Levites, priests in the house of the Lord doing the work of the Lord, and yet it says they knew not the Lord. Why? Because they did not keep the commandments true in their spirit; they kept it on the surface where you can see it. They looked the part: they had on the fringes, they had the beard, they showed up on the sabbath day; but their spirit was not right with the Lord, and they were really the sons of the devil. Do not let that be you, Israel.

The priests' custom with the people was that when any man offered sacrifice, the priest's servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand, and struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. They would dip it in, and what came up was the priest's portion of meat for that day; all the Levites did that, based on the sacrifices Israel brought in. This is how the Lord took care of Levi. He told Levi in the law that Levi would have no inheritance of land among the tribes; the Lord provided for them through the sacrifices that Israel brought, so they had need of nothing.

Also, before they burnt the fat, the priest's servant came and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw: I will cook it up my own way, give it to me now, before it is done. And if any man said, Let them not fail to burn the fat presently, and then take as much as thy soul desireth, he would answer, Nay; but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force. These were devils serving in the house of the Lord, strong-arming the offerings. Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the Lord: for men abhorred the offering of the Lord. These priests were disrespecting the offering of the Lord.

But Samuel ministered before the Lord, being a child, girded with a linen ephod; moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice. Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, The Lord give thee seed of this woman for the loan which is lent to the Lord. And the Lord visited Hannah, so that she conceived and bare three sons and two daughters; and the child Samuel grew before the Lord.

Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel, and how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: the harlots hanging around the temple, and Eli's sons dealing with them. He said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings by all this people; ye make the Lord's people to transgress. The Levites were the leaders, so the people followed their actions: what the priests did, the people did also. They saw the sons of Eli sleeping with the harlots and said, it must be all right, look what they have, look how they live in the temple; let us follow their lead. Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because the Lord would slay them. And the child Samuel grew on, and was in favour both with the Lord, and also with men. Eli might have said something to his children, but he did not remove them and put them out of the priesthood for their evil dealings; he said something, but he did not go further than words, he took no action with it. Watch what happened to his children.

There came a man of God unto Eli, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh's house? That is talking about Levi, going into Moses. Did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel? They had need of nothing; they were well taken care of. Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me? You are disrespecting me, is what he is saying: I am supposed to be honoured in everything before the children of Israel, and you let your sons disrespect my offerings. Take that into account: do you honour your children above what the Lord says to do? Can they do no wrong, even when they are doing real wrong against the Lord, keeping no commandments, never showing up on the sabbath day, and still living under your roof grown? If they are of age, they know right from wrong, and they are under your roof while you keep the commandments, then they had better be keeping the commandments: showing up to every feast day, the blowing of trumpets, the day of atonement, the passover, the same as you. When they are of age they can go their own way; but they should not be living under your roof and breaking the commandments of God. You honour your children above God when you allow that.

Wherefore the Lord God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the Lord saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed. Lightly esteemed means the Lord is not really looking out for you: you are not thinking about me, so I am not thinking about you; go ahead and see how it works out for yourself. That is why the Lord dealt with Abraham the way he did: Abraham was not going to choose his kids above the Most High, and they were going to do all that he commanded.

Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father's house, that there shall not be an old man in thine house. Cutting off the arm means cutting off thy strength: it was talking about his children. He was going to kill Eli's descendants young, and all the increase of his house would die in the flower of their age, in the full strength and peak of their youth. Why would the Lord judge the children of future generations of Eli's house? The thought might be, he is killing them for the sins of their forefather; I thought the sons did not die for the fathers. [Ezekiel 18](/bible/ezekiel/18) shows what it is talking about: the judgment falls on the son that continues in the sins of his father.

And this shall be a sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they shall die both of them. And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind; and I will build him a sure house, and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever. That is the same man we have to be: faithful unto the Lord, doing all that is in his heart and in his mind, not in our own. We cannot lean upon our own understanding, and we cannot lean upon our own emotions and how we feel; in whatever situation, at any given moment, it is what did the Lord say. Do not let the old man guide you and lead you; it should be the spirit of Christ which is in you, the hidden man.

It shall come to pass, that every one that is left in thine house shall come and crouch to him for a piece of silver and a morsel of bread. The Lord was going to make it hard on the descendants of Eli: he removed them from the priesthood, and it was written down that the descendants of Eli were not to be allowed into the house of the Lord any more. Remember, Levi was given no inheritance of land; so how would they eat, how would they live, how would they survive? Receiving their inheritance and their goods was based on them doing what thus saith the Lord told them to do, teaching the laws. Cut off from the priesthood, Eli's house was left to beg.

The child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision. Precious means the Lord was not dealing with everybody: he was not dealing with the priests, and there were no prophets around saying, thus saith the Lord. The word was about to go only to Samuel.

Eli was laid down in his place, his eyes beginning to wax dim, and ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, Samuel was laid down to sleep. Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out. That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out, though at a point in time it did go out.

The Lord called Samuel, and he answered, Here am I, and ran unto Eli; and Eli said, I called not; lie down again. The Lord called yet again, and again Samuel went to Eli. Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him. Look at that. Samuel had been in the house of the Lord since he was weaned, three or four years old, and he still did not know the Lord. This goes in on those playing church with their children: just because your children come and sit and listen to the teaching does not mean they know the Lord; they are there because you brought them there. They can hear all the words they want, but until the Lord reveals himself to them, they do not know him. What makes your kid so special, greater than Samuel? Do not have your children going into a covenant with Christ that he will judge them for if they break it; the scripture says, for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it: kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it; do not rush it.

The Lord called Samuel again the third time, and Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child; therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth. The Lord is merciful with us even in these days, in this wickedness: he calls out to us numerous times until we wake up. We do not know who is chosen, so we never know when we are going to wake up; it might be the first time, the second time, or the third time you hear the voice of the Lord calling. Some heard the call the first time because the Most High ordained them to be built up as leaders, to get the spirits of the world off of them so they could be a righteous example and a fit guide for you; you came in at the third call, after they were prepared. Your job is not to try to supersede those that came in before you, but to follow them; God set it up that way for a reason.

And the Lord came and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. The Lord did not just call from the heavens: the Lord came down and stood by Samuel and called out to him. That is cold-blooded. Samuel could not see him, but he heard him; that is what happens in the spirit to all of us. Notice in the scriptures that the Most High calls the name two times: Moses, Moses; Samuel, Samuel. That may be a question to ask Christ, Lord's will, for him that endures to the end. What was happening spiritually when the Most High was revealing himself to Samuel and about to pour his word into him? The same thing that happens to all Israel: he stands at the door and knocks. That door is your spirit. The knocking is the Lord calling out through the videos, the flyers, the four chapters a day, the classes; that is the Lord standing and knocking at the spirit of all Israel before he cuts you off.

The Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end. For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not. Eli let his children break the commandments of the Lord and lead the people astray, and he restrained them not. Therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever. When the Lord is mad, the Lord is mad: thus we are in the lands of our captivity 400 years and counting, and you have heard the history of the Spanish Inquisition, how we were burned for keeping the commandments; his anger burns unto the lowest hell. Do not let that be you. Do not let the Lord pass a judgment on your house where Christ prays for you and the Most High says, No, I will bring a judgment on his house for ever. Do not sin a sin so great that it cannot be prayed for, so that nothing is left but the fiery day of judgment.

Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord; and Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision. But Eli called him and said, What is the thing that the Lord hath said unto thee? I pray thee hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide any thing from me of all the things that he said unto thee. Samuel was going to be a judge of Israel, and here is his first test as a judge: do not sugarcoat what the Lord has said, and do not trim your words to seek love. And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. Eli said, It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good. Eli had no control of his kids, but he accepted the judgment of the Lord: thy will be done. Maybe the Lord had mercy on Eli; that is of the Lord, and we will not know.

Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground. What does that mean? What Samuel said, it came to pass. All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord. And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh: for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the Lord. That is good history we read today about Samuel; take heed to what you have heard, and do not let it slip. Some of you may be in these same situations: putting other people before God, honouring your children above God and not restraining them, or hearing the Lord call once, twice, three times without answering the call. This history is here for us to learn from; use it, lest the judgments of God be passed upon us when he is angry, for whatever the Most High says, Christ follows, because that is the order: God, Christ, man, woman, children.

He that is wounded in the stones or hath his privy member cut off shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord. This law repeats what was already given: the priests' law in Leviticus lists the same blemishes that barred a man from approaching to offer the bread of his God, including him that hath his stones broken.

A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to his tenth generation: the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. The prophets tie the bastard to Ashdod: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it. In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to their tenth generation, for ever. In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses in the audience of the people, and when they heard it our people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude whom they had intermarried with and had children with.

The reason for the ban: Ammon and Moab met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, and hired Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor to curse them. The history is in Numbers: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, was sore afraid because the people were many, and sent the elders of Moab and Midian with the rewards of divination to call Balaam to curse Israel. Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred: he shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, and as we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

When the host goeth forth against thine enemies, then keep thee from every wicked thing: when Israel went to war, they were to keep themselves from every wicked thing. The example is Achan: Israel was warned in any wise to keep from the accursed thing, lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it, and Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again.

There was a place without the camp to go forth abroad, and a paddle upon the weapon to dig and cover that which cometh from thee: to make it plain, if you had to ease yourself, you went outside the camp to do it. Verse 14 explains why: the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy, that he see no unclean thing in thee and turn away from thee. That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy.

There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel. A sodomite is the biblical word for a homosexual, and the whore of the daughters of Israel here is the same sin in the daughters, what we today would call lesbians. There is a heavy push in the world today for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians; popular entertainers are used to influence the younger generation to sin, just as young rappers were dressed in skirts and dresses until it became cool to be gay. This is what we have to bring our people back from: by being an example, the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves, and by having families, reinstituting a father and a mother in the divine order the Most High God established. Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord thy God, for even both these are abomination unto the Lord. Without are dogs: that is not the four-legged barking kind, but the other nations. Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother, usury of money, of victuals, of any thing: when you read the definition of usury, that is interest. We are not to charge interest to each other when we loan each other anything. Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury: the blessing is that Israel shall lend unto many nations and shall not borrow, the head and not the tail. That is our rightful place on the earth when we keep these commandments: we should lend unto them and may take usury upon what we lend to them, but we should not do that to our own people. The same law was already read in Exodus: if thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer.

text.text: So Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and after they had drunk. Now Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the Lord.
And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the Lord, and wept sore.

And she vowed a vow, and said, O Lord of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.
And it came to pass, as she continued praying before the Lord, that Eli marked her mouth.
Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken.
And Eli said unto her, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee.
And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the Lord.
Count not thine handmaid for a daughter of Belial: for out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.
Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.
And she said, Let thine handmaid find grace in thy sight. So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad.
And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before the Lord, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah: and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the Lord remembered her.
Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the Lord.

And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bullocks, and one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine, and brought him unto the house of the Lord in Shiloh: and the child was young.
And they slew a bullock, and brought the child to Eli.
And she said, Oh my lord, as thy soul liveth, my lord, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto the Lord.
For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him:
Therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord. And he worshipped the Lord there.
And Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the Lord, mine horn is exalted in the Lord: my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; because I rejoice in thy salvation.
There is none holy as the Lord: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.
Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.
They that were full have hired out themselves for bread; and they that were hungry ceased: so that the barren hath born seven; and she that hath many children is waxed feeble.
The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up.
The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.

He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them.
He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail.

The adversaries of the Lord shall be broken to pieces; out of heaven shall he thunder upon them: the Lord shall judge the ends of the earth; and he shall give strength unto his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed.
But Samuel ministered before the Lord, being a child, girded with a linen ephod.
Moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said, The Lord give thee seed of this woman for the loan which is lent to the Lord. And they went unto their own home.
And the Lord visited Hannah, so that she conceived, and bare three sons and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew before the Lord.
And Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground.
And all Israel from Dan even to Beer–sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord.
And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh: for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the Lord.
When thou shalt vow a vow unto the Lord thy God, thou shalt not slack to pay it: for the Lord thy God will surely require it of thee; and it would be sin in thee.
But if thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee.
That which is gone out of thy lips thou shalt keep and perform; even a freewill offering, according as thou hast vowed unto the Lord thy God, which thou hast promised with thy mouth.
